title: private-cp-edge-node-provisioning-and-rollback-notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working notes doc for provisioning 'edge' control-plane nodes in customer VPC / on-prem installs and a pragmatic rollback/rotation playbook. It is intentionally operational and terse — meant to be copied into runbooks and integrated with terraform modules and on-call playbooks. Focus areas: initial site prep, node sizing & capacity scenarios, terraform idempotency gotchas, safe upgrade sequence, immediate rollback steps, and verification checks.

Summary of the approach (short):
- Treat edge control-plane nodes as immutable units for day-to-day operations: provision via terraform, bootstrap via Ansible/systemd, and swap on rotation rather than in-place mutating binaries.
- Use staggered canary rotations by ring (canary -> ring1 -> ring2) using minimal traffic routing to avoid broad KV/cache churn.
- Keep a single rollback artifact per release (container image tag / tarball digest) and a documented ripcord command for emergency reverts.

Environment assumptions:
- Customer VPC with at least 3 subnets across 2 AZs (or equivalent on-prem racks).
- Control-plane cluster runs a small set of services: cp-api, cp-sync, cp-agent, cp-cache (kv-store), and cp-operator.
- Terraform state stored in a remote backend (s3-compatible or GCS) with locking (dynamodb/consul).
- Image registry accessible from site (with pull-through cache where recommended).

Initial site prep checklist (pre-provision):
- Confirm network CIDR allocations and NAT/egress paths documented.
- Validate customer firewall rules allow: 443 outgoing to registry, 22/SSH from ops network, and 9000-9100 for intra-cp HTTP tunnels.
- Create service account with scoped creds for terraform remote state and KMS (if using KMIP/KMS).
- Ensure time sync (chrony/ntpd) and baseline image hardening (security patch level) are agreed.
- Provision logging/metrics sink endpoints (remote ES cluster, DataDog forwarder, or graylog).

Node sizing and capacity scenarios (operational knobs):
- Small site (pilot): 2 control-plane nodes (m=8vCPU/32GB RAM) + 1 standby, expected ~50 req/s sustained.
- Medium site (production): 3-5 nodes (m=16vCPU/64GB), autoscale pool for stateless workers, expected ~200-800 req/s with batching.
- High-throughput (dedicated): 6+ nodes with GPU-backed inference routers and dedicated KV cache cluster.
Notes: CPU/RAM skewing depends heavily on per-request sequence length distribution and KV cache hit ratio. Keep headroom for GC/heap spikes.

Terraform module notes (scratch):
- Use stable module versions (pin to exact tag) in customer manifests. Avoid "latest" module references.
- Example snippet (reference to copy into customer manifests):
  module "cp_edge_node" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//cp-edge-node?ref=v1.6.2"
    name_prefix = var.name_prefix
    instance_type = var.instance_type
    subnet_ids = var.controlplane_subnet_ids
    ami_id = var.ami_cp_base
    kubelet_token = var.bootstrap_token
    tags = merge(var.common_tags, {"env" = var.env, "role" = "controlplane"})
  }
- Idempotency gotcha: cloud-init/user-data scripts that write files with timestamps can make terraform think instances changed. When authoring cloud-init, use deterministic content or write via prebuilt AMI baker pipeline.
- State drift: Use periodic terraform plan-time drift reports (CI job) and alert if plan changes > 3 resources.

Bootstrap / post-provision steps (automated + manual):
- Automated: cloud-init registers node with internal PKI, pulls docker images, and registers to service discovery.
- Manual verification checklist (first 10 minutes):
  - SSH into node (jumpbox) and check systemctl status for cp-agent and cp-operator.
  - tail -n 200 /var/log/cp-agent.log for recent startup errors.
  - curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz (service-level health).
  - confirm KV cache warmed (curl to local cache endpoint and check hit rates).
  - run smoke generation script on canary route (~5-10 qps) to validate latency tail.

Rotation and upgrade plan (canary -> progressive):
1) Prepare release artifact (container image or OS package) and publish to registry with immutable digest.
2) Create an Upgrade Run in the console (or runbook) that lists nodes in ring order and target artifact digest.
3) Canary: pick 1 node in canary ring, cordon + drain user traffic (if applicable), and deploy artifact via rollout system (or run the ansible playbook to update the unit).
4) Run functional smoke tests and the evals harness against canary node for a minimum of 30 minutes (longer for heavy state migrations).
5) If OK, bump to ring1 using parallelism=2 and watch metrics for 60 minutes; continue to ring2.
6) After full rollout, run a full traffic soak at expected peak for 2 hours and verify 99.9th latency within SLO.

Key metrics to monitor during upgrade (thresholds are site-specific; use these as starting points):
- HTTP 5xx rate: alert if > 0.5% for > 5 minutes during rollout.
- Tail latency (p99): alert if > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes.
- KV miss surge: alert if cache miss rate increases by 3x baseline.
- Error budget burn: if rollout incrementally uses > 25% of remaining error budget, pause.

Rollback (fast ripcord) steps:
- When to trigger: sustained 5xx > 1% OR p99 > 3x baseline for > 15 minutes OR operator judgement.
- Immediate actions:
  1) Pause rollout system and mark release as suspended.
  2) For each affected ring, trigger automated rollback to the previous artifact digest: example ripcord command: 
     cpctl rollout rollback --site $SITE --service controlplane --to-digest sha256:abcd1234 --rings canary,ring1 --parallel 2
  3) If automated tooling not available, revert via terraform by provisioning replacement nodes pinned to previous AMI/instance config, update service discovery to point at replacements, and decommission upgraded nodes.
  4) Lower traffic to site-level reduced mode: switch traffic to fallback region or reduce client QPS via token bucket at API gateway.
  5) Open incident in PagerDuty and note exact trigger metrics and affected digests.

Post-rollback follow-up:
- Capture logs (journalctl and container logs) for 1h before and after rollback and attach to incident.
- Run git bisect style deploy if the failure is suspected to be configuration drift: try previous artifact, then step forward.
- Add replay of failing requests to an isolated test harness for root cause analysis.

Special considerations for on-prem / air-gapped sites:
- Ensure local registry mirror and signed artifacts. Keep a documented offline media procedure (USB / local repo) for emergency reverts.
- KMS/HSM: test rekeying flows in a staging mirror first. Avoid rekey during upgrades.
- Limited bandwidth: prefer binary deltas for OS upgrades and teach the installer to resume interrupted pulls.

Common failure modes & recovery notes (field notes):
- Cloud-init infinite loop: re-image node and ensure userdata idempotency, then re-run.
- KV cluster partitioning observed after rotation: increase gossip timeouts, roll quorum nodes first, and avoid simultaneous restarts of majority nodes.
- Metrics disappearance after upgrade: check forwarder endpoint auth (token rotation) and restart collector agent.

Runbook snippets (copyable):
- Verify node health: systemctl is-active cp-agent || journalctl -u cp-agent -n 200
- Drain node (k8s-style): cpctl node cordon $NODE && cpctl node drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Deploy artifact (ansible): ansible-playbook -i inventory/prod cp-deploy.yml -e image_digest=sha256:abcd1234
- Emergency revert (terraform replace pattern): terraform apply -var 'node_image=ami-previous' -target=module.cp_edge_node["edge-3"]

Open questions / TODOs (for final runbook):
- Decide canonical ring definitions for small vs large sites (how many rings?)
- Standardize on ripcord CLI and make it a privileged operation only via a small set of SRE roles.
- Add automated smoke/eval harness integration to block rollout on regressions rather than manual pause.
- Define exact state migration steps for KV schema changes and test in lab.

Appendix: useful links and references:
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-private/pull/482
- Terraform modules: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/tree/main/cp-edge-node
- Related Jira: JIRA-CP-1297 (edge node rotation improvements)

Notes on tone: this is intentionally raw — copy relevant sections into the customer-facing runbook and refine the precise commands per customer environment. Keep this doc as the developer scratchpad for future runbook consolidation.
